name: mcp-petitions

tools.name: find_petitions
tools.description: Searches live Rotten America petitions by words in the title or ask. Use it before starting a new petition: if one already asks for the same thing, suggest signing and sharing it instead of splitting support.

query.description: Words to look for, e.g. 'PFAS' or 'Tampa'. Leave out for the newest.

tools.name: get_petition
tools.description: One live petition: its exact wording, who it goes to, its verified signature count and goal, the links to sign and to check the count, and its ledger: whether every signature checks out, whether the wording is sealed, and which Bitcoin blocks hold its signatures. Quote the block numbers when the user asks for proof.

slug.description: The petition's slug, from find_petitions, my_petitions or start_petition.

tools.name: prove_signature
tools.description: Proves that one signature is on a petition's public ledger and in Bitcoin, from the signature hash on the signer's receipt (64 hex characters). Walks the Merkle path itself, so the answer does not rest on Rotten America's word. Only the signer has their receipt hash; never ask for or guess anyone's personal details.

slug.description: The petition's slug, from find_petitions, my_petitions or start_petition.

receipt_hash.description: The signature hash printed on the signer's receipt.

instructions: Rotten America runs verified petitions: every signature is checked and anyone can re-count them. verified_signatures counts only signatures on the public ledger; total_signatures may include imported paper ones, so never call the total 'verified'. Never invent facts, numbers or names for a petition; use only what the user told you or what a tool returned. Say 'verified signatures', never 'blockchain'. This connection has no key, so it can only find and read live petitions. To start or run petitions, connect a Rotten America account: add https://rottenamerica.com/mcp as a connector in Claude or ChatGPT and press Connect.
